title: Linkability of registration data
description: Home Hub may link account and device data with other user activities, enabling profiling.

title: Identifiability of homeowner
description: Home Hub can identify the homeowner from registration data.

title: Non-repudiation of registration action
description: Homeowner cannot deny account registration if Home Hub logs the action.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of sensitive data
description: Home Hub may expose account or device details to unauthorized parties.

title: Data integrity violation in transit
description: Registration data could be altered during transmission to Home Hub.

title: Unawareness of data processing
description: Homeowner may not be aware of how their data is used beyond registration.

title: Lack of notice about data processing
description: Homeowner is not informed about data processing activities by Home Hub.

title: Access code interception during transmission
description: The temporary access code transmitted from Guest User to Home Hub could be intercepted by an eavesdropper monitoring the communication channel, allowing unauthorized access to the front door.
assumptions: The communication between Guest User and Home Hub is not encrypted or uses weak encryption

title: Access code stored insecurely at Home Hub
description: The Home Hub may store the temporary access code in an insecure manner (e.g., plaintext logs, unencrypted database), allowing unauthorized parties to retrieve past or current access codes.
assumptions: Home Hub stores access codes for audit or verification purposes

title: Guest presence detectable through access code entry
description: An observer could detect that a guest is present at the property by observing the act of entering an access code at the Home Hub, revealing the guest's participation in the system.
assumptions: The access code entry is visible to observers (e.g., keypad display, physical interaction)

title: Guest identifiable from access code
description: The Home Hub could link the temporary access code to a specific guest's identity, enabling identification of who accessed the property and when.
assumptions: Access codes are unique per guest or linked to guest identity in the system

title: Guest activities linkable through access logs
description: The Home Hub could link multiple access events to the same guest, creating a profile of their visit patterns and frequency.
assumptions: Home Hub maintains access logs that can be correlated across time

title: Linkability of sensor events to individuals
description: Motion, door, and sensor events written by the Home Hub can be linked to specific individuals' movements and behaviors within the home, creating detailed activity profiles.
assumptions: Sensor events contain timestamps and location data that can be correlated with individual presence

title: Identifiability from sensor event patterns
description: Patterns in motion and door events can identify specific individuals based on their movement patterns, daily routines, and presence in different rooms.
assumptions: Event data contains sufficient granularity to distinguish between different household members

title: Unawareness of event logging
description: Users may not be aware that motion, door, and sensor events are being continuously logged and stored, potentially violating informed consent principles.
assumptions: Users are not explicitly informed about the scope and purpose of event logging

title: Unauthorized access to event log
description: The Local Event Log storing motion/door/sensor events could be accessed by unauthorized parties, revealing detailed information about household activities and occupancy patterns.
assumptions: Event log has insufficient access controls or is stored without encryption

title: Tampering with event log data
description: The Local Event Log could be modified or tampered with, allowing false events to be recorded or legitimate events to be deleted, compromising data integrity.
assumptions: Event log lacks integrity protection mechanisms like hashing or write-once storage

title: Linkability through stored event history
description: Historical event data in the Local Event Log can be analyzed to link individuals to specific times, locations, and activities over extended periods.
assumptions: Event log retains sufficient historical data for pattern analysis

title: Linkability of video uploads to user identity
description: Home Hub may include metadata (e.g., device ID, timestamps) that links uploaded video clips to a specific user or household, enabling tracking of user activity.
assumptions: Metadata is included in uploads without anonymization

title: Identifiable information in video content
description: Recorded camera clips may contain personally identifiable information (e.g., faces, license plates) that can be used to identify individuals.
assumptions: Video content is not processed to remove identifiable features before upload

title: Unauthorized interception of video data in transit
description: Video clips transmitted from Home Hub to cloud storage could be intercepted if the communication channel is not properly secured (e.g., unencrypted or weak encryption).
assumptions: Data flow uses standard encryption without additional security measures

title: Deduction of sensitive user habits from stored videos
description: Cloud storage may analyze or aggregate video data to infer sensitive information about user routines, presence, or behavior patterns.
assumptions: Cloud provider performs automated analysis on stored video content

title: User unawareness of data sharing
description: Users may not be adequately informed that their recorded video clips are being uploaded to cloud storage, violating transparency expectations.
assumptions: Privacy notices or consent mechanisms are unclear or absent

title: Excessive exposure of motion alert data to backend
description: Motion alert data may be shared with third parties beyond necessary scope, violating the minimality principle. The backend could expose personal data (e.g., location, device ID) to external parties not anticipated at design time.
assumptions: Backend processes motion alerts without strict data minimization controls.

title: Identifiability via motion alert data in transit
description: Motion alert data in transit could be intercepted, allowing identification of the user or device through metadata (e.g., timestamps, device identifiers).
assumptions: Data flow lacks encryption or secure transmission protocols.
uncertainty_note: Tree node I.1.1 inferred from standard LINDDUN knowledge; context did not specify I threat nodes.

title: Linkability of motion alerts to user profile
description: Backend may correlate motion alerts with other data (e.g., user activity logs) to build detailed user profiles, enabling tracking across contexts.
assumptions: Backend retains and processes motion alert data alongside other user data.
uncertainty_note: Tree node L.1.1 inferred from standard LINDDUN knowledge; context did not specify L threat nodes.

title: Motion detection data disclosure at source
description: The mobile app backend (P2) shares motion detection event information with the homeowner, disclosing when and where motion was detected in their property. This reveals occupancy patterns and security system activity.
assumptions: Motion detection data is considered sensitive personal information about the homeowner's property and presence patterns.

title: Notification interception in transit
description: The motion-detected notification traveling from backend to homeowner's phone could be intercepted, revealing when motion events occur and potentially the homeowner's location/presence status.
assumptions: The notification flow may not be fully encrypted or could be vulnerable to network-level attacks.

title: Linkability through notification timing
description: The timing and frequency of motion notifications could be monitored to link the homeowner's presence/absence patterns, creating a profile of when they are home versus away.
assumptions: Third parties could monitor notification delivery patterns to infer occupancy.

title: Notification history aggregation
description: The homeowner's phone stores notification history, which could be aggregated over time to create detailed profiles of motion events, occupancy patterns, and daily routines.
assumptions: Notification data is stored locally on the device and could be accessed or exfiltrated.

title: Unawareness of data sharing scope
description: The homeowner may be unaware of what metadata accompanies motion notifications (e.g., timestamps, sensor IDs, location data) that the backend shares beyond the basic alert.
assumptions: Users typically don't examine technical details of notification payloads.

title: Violation of storage limitation principle
description: Video clips stored in cloud storage may be retained longer than necessary for the homeowner's playback needs, violating data minimization and storage limitation principles.
assumptions: Cloud storage system does not have automatic deletion policies based on retention requirements

title: Unauthorized disclosure during data transfer
description: Video data in transit between cloud storage and mobile app backend could be intercepted by unauthorized parties if encryption is not properly implemented.
assumptions: Data flow may not use end-to-end encryption or may have weak encryption implementation

title: Linkability through retrieval metadata
description: Metadata about video retrieval requests (timestamps, video IDs, user identifiers) could be used to link and profile homeowner behavior patterns.
assumptions: Request metadata is logged and potentially accessible to third parties or could be correlated across systems

title: Data misuse beyond intended purpose
description: Mobile app backend could process or use retrieved video data for purposes beyond homeowner playback, such as analytics, advertising, or sharing with third parties.
assumptions: Backend system has capabilities to process video data beyond simple retrieval and playback

title: Unawareness of data processing
description: Homeowner may not be aware when their video clips are being retrieved and processed by the backend, or for what specific purposes beyond playback.
assumptions: User interface does not provide clear notifications or transparency about video retrieval events
